body.html:
Cloud Console Hardening wave 2 — ship the train: the four lies leave the wire, and the ledger stops lying about wave 1

Living wave Paper for the Cloud Console Hardening epic (bp task cloud-console-hardening-epic, 91 children, 80 open). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-console-hardening-charter.md - the epic's law, carrying standing laws 1-6 and decisions D1-D24 ratified by wave 1. This is the epic's FIRST wave Paper: wave 1 ran before the Paper convention was applied here, so its story lives in the charter and in the perfected task rows. Phases append below in order; someone opening this mid-wave sees exactly where the wave stands.

STATUS: SURVEYING. Strategize is complete and has opened the wave; the survey fleet flies next. Nothing is decided until Decide appends below, after two rounds of exploration.

The wish

"cloud-console-hardening WAVE 2 - FINISH THE FOUR LIES ON THE WIRE. Wave 1 established the frame (the console tells people things that are not true) and shipped five slices. Wave 2 takes the ones wave 1 named but did not close, led by the SSE bearer-token ticket and the HEAD sweep." Model constraint (hard): every phase runs on Opus/Sonnet; Decide MUST set builder_model:'opus' for EVERY slice, never 'fable'.

The finding that reframes this wave

The brief says wave 1 SHIPPED five slices, and instructs me to verify each landed by content on origin/main before building on it. I did. Most of it did not land.

•
•
•
•
•
•

And the SSE leak is fully live on main, both legs, exactly as wave 1 measured it: cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex:9707 reads `Auth.bearer_token(conn) || conn.query_params["token"]`, and cloud/priv/static/app.js:11919 constructs `new EventSource("/v1/events?token=" + encodeURIComponent(s.token))`. Nothing has moved.

So the ledger says wave 1 shipped; origin/main says it did not. That is a claim/reality divergence - which is precisely this epic's own triage predicate, turned on the epic itself. The console stops lying; so must the wave log.

The gate truth, measured

The stranded PRs are not blocked on quality. `gh pr checks` on #5305 and #5309 shows failures ONLY on advisory or known-systemically-broken checks: Format (explicitly labelled advisory), the Vercel deploys (this epic already carries the row gr-blk-vercel-checks-ungoverned recording that Vercel fails on every PR repo-wide), and on #5309 Sobelow (the repo's standing stale-baseline condition, which reds on main itself). Only #5290 carries genuine reds. Two of the three headline blockers are minutes of lead work, not a build round.

The direction: SHIP THE TRAIN

Wave 2's definition of done is not "five good branches exist." It is: the four lies are gone FROM THE RUNNING SYSTEM on origin/main. The wave's deliverable is an ordered merge train, and the wave owns landing wave 1's residue as well as its own slices. Four movements.

Movement 0 - land the stranded (lead-owned, off the critical path)

Drive #5305, #5307, #5308 and #5309 to merge on their advisory reds, per the repo's standing 'required gates pass -> merge' law; fix #5290's genuine reds as a small slice. Verify each BY CONTENT after merge, never by PR state. This unblocks router.ex and app.js - but crucially it does NOT gate movement 1.

Movement 1 - the two headliners, built in PARALLEL from origin/main

cch-w2-head-sideeffect-fence and cch-w3-sse-ticket. Both already carry perfected briefs with L1 measured evidence and ratified decisions (D8-D16). Builders EXECUTE; they do not re-decide. I am rejecting wave 1's declared serialization: the 'AFTER X merges' notes are file-truth about textual conflict, not semantic dependency, and the edit sites are far apart - HEAD's deny-list plug sits before router.ex:284, peer-ip at :377, SSE at :9707; refetch touches app.js:12076 and SSE app.js:11919. Git merges these. The ordering cost is paid once, at merge time, by the lead - not by three serialized build rounds.

Movement 2 - the honest harness (disjoint surface, zero collision)

gr-blk-revoke-harness-gap plus gr-blk-smoke-click-inert as ONE deliverable, as the charter already rules: a click oracle scoped to the dangerous buttons. Today scenarios.mjs has an explicit handler for GET /v1/account/sessions but NONE for either DELETE, so both revoke paths fall through to a generic 200 and the toast reads '0 session(s) revoked' - a false green on a destructive control, inside an epic whose named enemy is the false green. This touches scenarios.mjs and smoke.mjs and collides with nothing else in the wave.

Movement 3 - the sibling sweep, and a new standing law

Every one of wave 1's five slices spawned a residue row of the same shape: cch-w2-ledger-close-guard-create-ops (the guard covered two patch clauses; createOrReplace/replace is a THIRD open door), cch-w1-mirror-direct-write-unfenced (the emit fence holds in emit.mjs but the paper-editor mirror bypasses it), cch-w1-emit-fence-regression-test, cch-bl-overview-subscription-band-stale, cch-bl-overview-background-refresh-fails-silently, and cch-bl-cssom-floor-decays-as-css-grows.

That is not six unrelated misses. It is one pattern: the fix was scoped to the instance that was OBSERVED, not to the class that exists. It is the same shape as the lead's co-scoped finding - the HEAD honesty fix (#4481) CREATED the oauth mint exposure - and it is a claim/reality divergence in its own right, because a closed row that covers two of three doors is a ledger that lies. Proposed new charter law: every slice states, in evidence, the CLASS its fix covers and the siblings it does NOT. Cheap, mechanical, and it stops wave 3 from re-discovering wave 1's residue. Build cch-w2-ledger-close-guard-create-ops this wave as the pattern's first payment.

The joint-defect trap, named up front

The two headline slices can jointly create a defect - exactly the co-scoped pattern this epic already got bitten by. If the SSE ticket's mint route were a GET, the HEAD deny-list and the ticket design collide: a HEAD probe would mint AND burn a strictly-single-use ticket. The mint route MUST be a POST - which is also the house convention (router.ex already carries post "/v1/auth/login", "/v1/auth/device/start", "/v1/auth/reset" and nine more). The HEAD deny-list is the standing proof that it must stay a POST. Naming this before the builders fly is far cheaper than discovering it at merge.

The dark crown, restated

PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS is unset on prod, lives in a gitignored .env, and zero deploy scripts reference it - no commit can set it. It is a human gate belonging to the repo owner (gr-ops-platform-admin-emails). Same disposition for the QR live-scan (gr-backlog-qr-live-scan-proof). Note where relevant; never build around it, fake it, or file work that depends on it being lit.

Surface fence

In fence: cloud/, api/lib/barkpark_web/live/. Standing narrow dispensations from wave 1: api/lib/barkpark/content/mutations.ex and its tests, design/emit.mjs and design/check.mjs, and .github/workflows/console-harness.yml. Hands off: tooling/grip/ (truth-grip wave 5 RUNNING - PR #5314 is live right now) and scripts/pds-* plus api/lib/barkpark/tenancy/ (PDS wave 15 RUNNING). Movement 3's ledger work needs the existing mutations.ex dispensation and nothing wider. Any new dispensation is requested explicitly at Decide, out loud.

The direction debate

Rival A - 'land first, then build'

Serialize honestly: spend round 1 merging wave 1, then build HEAD, then SSE, respecting every declared dependency. Safest merge story. Rejected because it accepts wave 1's serialization as correctness when it is only file-adjacency, and it spends the wave's entire critical path on janitorial work - the four lies would stay on the wire another wave. The user asked to FINISH them.

Rival B - 'stack on the merge train'

Branch the headliners off the open PR branches so the declared dependencies are literally satisfied. Fastest to a working tree, and genuinely tempting. Rejected hard: it violates charter LAW 6 (cut every branch from origin/main explicitly), and it is the precise mechanism that stranded wave 1 in the first place - stacked branches whose parents never merged. Building on unmerged work is how this repo loses work.

Rival C - 'the dependencies are file-truth, not correctness-truth' - WINNER

Build the headliners in parallel from origin/main; pay the ordering cost once, at merge, lead-owned; run movement 0 concurrently as cheap lead work rather than as a gating round. Won because it is the only rival that both finishes the named lies AND lands wave 1, and because the measurement supports it: the edit sites are hundreds to thousands of lines apart in both hot files.

The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it

ATTACK: 'Clean git merges are exactly what hides a joint defect. This epic's own headline slice exists BECAUSE two individually-correct fixes composed into a vulnerability. Parallel building plus clean merges is the machine that manufactures that failure - you are optimising for the thing that already bit you.'

This is the strongest objection and I accept its force rather than hedging the direction. The wave absorbs it by paying an explicit price. (1) The joint-defect trap is named up front - the mint route is a POST, stated before any builder flies. (2) The merge train ends with a COMPOSITE proof round that exercises the four fixes together on merged main, not each fix alone on its own branch - because per this repo's own standing lesson, git merge-base is not evidence of behaviour. (3) The new sibling-class law makes every slice declare its uncovered siblings, which is the generalised form of the same defence. A second objection - 'you are overriding a ratified sequencing decision on a hunch' - is fair, and is not answered by argument: it becomes survey questions, and if the survey finds a genuinely shared function or a semantic coupling between HEAD and SSE, Decide serialises those two and keeps the rest parallel.

Survey plan

The survey fleet flies next. Width is cheap here and buys precise depth later. Every load-bearing assumption in the direction above is represented below, and each assignment says how its answer changes the plan. Digest appends the survey digest and the verify plan to this Paper BEFORE the verifiers fly.

The whole peer-ip change is ONE hunk (@@ -349,34 +349,81 @@), so plug(Plug.Head) stays at 284 unchanged and everything below shifts exactly +47. Wave 1's 'AFTER X merges' notes were file-adjacency, not semantic dependency. Rival C stands; D25 retires the serialization.

The sharpest attack, and what the wave pays for it

The attack was: 'clean git merges are exactly what HIDES a joint defect — this epic's headline slice exists BECAUSE two individually-correct fixes composed into a vulnerability.' Verification made that attack sharper, not weaker, and it is answered by three explicit payments rather than by argument.

Decisions (D25-D40 — mirrored from the charter)

The wave plan

Round 1 builds this run. Round 2 does NOT — the lead dispatches each after its dependency MERGES. Every slice is builder_model opus (Fable 5 is spend-limited this cycle).

Round 1's four slices are file-disjoint except router.ex, which SSE and HEAD touch ~8,400 lines apart. Merging #5305 first shifts SSE's coordinates +47 and leaves HEAD's unchanged — both briefs tell the builder to grep for anchors, never trust a line number.

Movement 0 — lead-owned, off the critical path

Merge #5305, #5308, #5309 on advisory reds. No PR carries a real red: #5309's Sobelow is the stale-baseline line drift that reproduces on main itself (5/5 of the last api-touching commits). Verify BY CONTENT after merge, never by PR state. Then take the free ledger close nobody has taken: gr-blk-emit-marker-fence AND cch-w1-emit-marker-fence criterion 6, citing merge SHA 60a4f90efa1bed4cb5eecade5a57a0f246b3d589 and design/emit.mjs:2099 — the census row was never touched by cch-w1-census-disposition, so nobody closed either.

Backlog filed this wave

REVIEW / DEBRIEF - 2026-07-21: what shipped, what the integration caught, and the grade

Closing section. One Fable reviewed all four green slices adversarially in an isolated worktree, chased each builder's own stated doubts first, fixed what was wrong in place, re-ran every gate, and audited the ledger. Round 1 built 4 slices; all 4 are green, reviewed and merge-ready. Rounds 2+ did not build BY DESIGN under the sequenced-rounds law, so their absence is not a stall.

What shipped, per slice

The joint defect the wave predicted - on an axis it did not

The Decide phase named the joint-defect trap up front and was RIGHT to: it forced the mint route to be a POST, and that specific collision (a HEAD probe minting and burning a single-use ticket) never happened. But a different one did, and it was invisible to every per-slice gate. The SSE slice raises a 'Live updates interrupted' toast when the ticket mint fails. In the preview harness the mint had no fixture, so it fell through to the benign generic /v1/ 200 {} - ok, but carrying no ticket - and the SPA read that as a failed mint. That toast had always been raised; it only became OBSERVABLE once the oracle slice gave the shim a real innerHTML and isConnected. At that point it broke account-modal-2fa-badcode, whose entire assertion is that a field error fires NO toast. Both slices were green alone. Only merging all four and re-running the full gate set surfaced it.

DATED CORRECTION to the 'joint-defect trap' section above (added at review, 2026-07-21): that section is not wrong, but it is narrower than the risk turned out to be. It reasoned about two slices colliding on the same ROUTE. The collision that actually occurred was between a slice that added a new failure TOAST and a slice that made toasts observable - disjoint files, disjoint surfaces, no shared route. The generalised lesson is now in the charter: per-slice green is not wave green, and an integration re-run of the full gate set across the merged wave is mandatory, not optional.

FIXED on the oracle's -r branch by fixturing POST /v1/auth/sse-ticket to return a real ticket. The sandbox's EventSource is already an inert stub, so a successful mint leaves the stream silent and deterministic. Modelled, not suppressed - an absent fixture would itself have been a lie about what the console does at boot. The fix is merge-order-independent: the fixture is inert on the oracle branch alone.

Verification actually run at review

Ledger audit

The builder ledger discipline this wave was excellent and is worth recording as the standard. All four tasks sit in_progress (never done), each claimed by its builder, each with an honest now-line naming the commit and the unpushed state. Every non-merge-gated criterion is stamped with substantial evidence - 500 to 1900 characters each, citing file:line and mutation results - and every task leaves its final MERGE-GATED criterion unmet for the lead, exactly per standing law 5. Two builders reported figures they could NOT reproduce (the GET census, the 57/36 drift count) as unreconciled rather than restating what they were handed, and filed rows to settle them. That is the opposite of the false-done pattern this charter exists to stop.

Grade: A-

Earned, not awarded. What genuinely carries it: the two headline slices closed real credential leaks and both are proven able to fail by MUTATION rather than merely green - seven independent mutations on the SSE slice, three directions on the HEAD fence including the over-broad direction a prefix guard would have taken. The click oracle's decisive mutation is the sharpest artifact of the wave, because it demonstrates the 9,074-line source-string suite is structurally blind to a dead button. And the honesty discipline is unusually high: builders corrected a wrong acceptance criterion against upstream source, refused to restate a census they could not reproduce, and wrote coverage BOUNDARIES into the shipped code rather than only into the ledger.

What holds it below an A. The wave shipped a cross-slice defect that no per-slice gate could see, and it was caught only because review integrated all four - had the lead merged on per-slice green, the harness would have gone red on main. One slice shipped duplicate object keys. Three significant proofs remain one layer up from the thing they certify: the SSE reconnect is proven in a node vm with a stubbed EventSource and never in a real browser (Safari is untested and has historically diverged here), the single-use guarantee is proven SEQUENTIALLY so the FOR UPDATE lock that actually serialises it is not exercised, and the Sobelow re-pin is an inference from a CI artifact that cannot be verified until it merges. Each is honestly flagged by its builder - which is why this is an A- and not lower - but flagged is not proven. Nothing here is bloat: every slice is the size of its problem, and the largest diff is mostly tests.
